title: A Field Scenario File: One Text File for the Ground, the Walls, the Goals and the Faults, Parsed With Every Mistake Reported at Once

questions.question: Why is a test better as a file than as a function?
options: A file is parsed faster than code is compiled
A function cannot hold walls and patches
It can be kept, shared, repeated and given to another simulator
A file needs no checking
questions.explanation: The same file gives the built in simulator its terrain and, later, Gazebo its world. A test written as code belongs to one program.

questions.question: A file with six mistakes gave how many reports?
options: 6, one for each mistake
1, the first
8, with their lines, six for lines and two for the whole file
15, one for each line
questions.explanation: Each bad line was reported with its number, and the two rules about the whole file, a duration and a start, were reported after the last line.

questions.question: Where is the check that a file has a start made?
options: On the first line
When the start line is read
When the simulator loads the file
After the last line, because it concerns the whole file
questions.explanation: A missing start is not a fault of any one line. It can only be known once every line has been read.

questions.question: What is the result of parsing, writing, parsing and writing?
options: The second text is shorter
The same text twice
The numbers lose a digit each time
The comments move to the top
questions.explanation: Written in a fixed order, a scenario that is parsed and written again comes out the same. That shows nothing is lost between the file and the structure.

questions.question: Why report a line number and the word that was wrong?
options: So the mistake can be found and fixed in one pass
To make the parser longer
So the file can be rejected sooner
Because the keywords are in English
questions.explanation: Six mistakes found one at a time are six runs. Reported together, each with its line and the offending word, they are fixed in one.

questions.question: Why are angles in a scenario in degrees but in code in radians?
options: Degrees are more exact
The parser cannot read a decimal point
Radians cannot express a right angle
A person writes 90, and the conversion is made once at the edge
questions.explanation: A person types 90 without thinking and 1.5708 with a calculator. The file is for the person and the code for the arithmetic.
